newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria blames fuel scarcity on faulty refineries.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria blames fuel scarcity on faulty refineries.

text.p: Oil minister Dan Etete said a current fuel shortage in Lagos was caused by faulty refineries and denied that the government planned to raise pump prices.
"The current problem is caused by slight faults at the Warri and Port Harcourt refineries, and we know the cause of the problem," Etete told airport reporters on Tuesday.
"By the end of this week the fuel problem will be solved."
He said $300 million was needed to rehabilitate Nigeria's ageing refineries, adding that maintenance work would commence at the Kaduna refinery in the north in July.
In the past fuel price increases have been preceded by similar scarcities, giving rise to speculations that the latest scarcity is a prelude to a price hike.

Nigeria has been under pressure from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund to raise the price of petrol, currently 11 naira a litre, as one of the conditions for endorsing a medium term economic reform programme that would qualify Nigeria for relief on its $28 billion external debt.
There were signs the scarcity could ease soon in Lagos, Nigeria's commercial hub, with arrival of two vessels carrying 29,162.36 metric tonnes of petrol at the Apapa Port on Tuesday.

Newspapers, quoting officials of Pipelines and Petroleum Marketing Company, a subsidiary of state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, reported on Wednesday that two more vessels were being expected in Lagos with fuel from Port Harcourt refinery in the southeast.
